subject.title: [Bug]: tasks maintenance can prune cron-run sessions after cron state restore failure

question: When persisted cron state cannot be restored, should `tasks maintenance --apply` abort the whole maintenance pass, or continue only maintenance operations that cannot prune session registry entries?
rationale: Both choices can be safe if implemented carefully, but they differ in operator expectations and in whether one command may partially apply maintenance while reporting degraded cron-state visibility.

options.title: Abort the whole apply pass
options.body: Fail before any maintenance mutation when cron state cannot be restored, matching the conservative task-flow restore gate.

options.title: Skip only dependent pruning
options.body: Continue task and task-flow maintenance only after proving those mutations do not depend on cron running-state restoration, while skipping session-registry pruning and reporting the partial result.

recommendation.title: Abort the whole apply pass
recommendation.body: Fail before any maintenance mutation when cron state cannot be restored, matching the conservative task-flow restore gate.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged session-maintenance work is the closest recent ownership signal for the shared lifecycle invariant.
